overview: 1.b3 b5 mirrors White's queenside flank play. White usually continues 2.Bb2 (or 2.e4) with the bishop hitting the long diagonal and e5 central control. The extra b5 by Black weakens c6 and the queenside, and White can strike with e4 or a3. It is rarely played by strong players.

white_ideas.idea: Develop Bb2 and e3/e4 with central control
Play a3 and c4 to open lines against the b5 advance

typical_structures.structure: Mutual fianchetto on the long diagonals
White centre pawns e4/d4 against Black flank play

character.notes: Slow flank play; tactics only after the centre opens.

soundness.notes: 1...b5 is slightly weakening but not refuted.

structure.notes: Fianchetto bishops with central pawns undecided.

approach.notes: Black rarely plays 1...b5 against 1.b3 at a high level.

character.reason: Slow flank play with chances for both and no forced lines.

structure.reason: Centre is undecided as in all flank openings.

plans.reason: Bb2 on the long diagonal and queenside pawns.
